hints.title: Rightmost Inversion Point
hints.text: To find the largest permutation smaller than arr, identify the rightmost index i such that arr[i] > arr[i + 1]. If no such index exists, the array is in non-decreasing order and cannot be reduced.

hints.title: Largest Smaller Swap Candidate
hints.text: Look to the right of index i for the maximum value strictly smaller than arr[i]. If that maximum value appears multiple times, choose its leftmost occurrence.

hints.title: Single Swap Execution
hints.text: Swap arr[i] with the chosen candidate element arr[j]. The resulting array is guaranteed to be the lexicographically greatest permutation smaller than the input.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: number of elements in arr
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all O(N^2) possible pairwise swaps is inefficient and unnecessary.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Scanning backwards to locate index i and forward to pick best j takes O(N) time and modifies arr in-place.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should find the first descending pair from the right and pick the largest strictly smaller value to swap.
complexity.notes: Duplicate maximum values in the suffix must select the earliest instance to maximize order.
